title: How to Increase Average Order Value in Retail Stores | Entuned
meta_description: Proven strategies to increase average transaction value in physical retail, including the overlooked role of in-store music and sound.

faq.q: What are the standard ways to increase AOV in physical retail?
faq.a: The three proven tactics are cross-merchandising (placing complementary products near each other), staff-driven upselling (suggesting a second item at the point of decision), and threshold incentives (spend $75 get free gift wrapping). All three work but none address the ambient environment customers make decisions inside of.

faq.q: How does music tempo affect how much customers spend?
faq.a: Published research consistently finds that slower tempos in minor keys increase time in store and correlate with higher total spend. Genre congruence — music that fits the store's brand — increases customers' willingness to pay premium prices.

faq.q: Can lyrics in store music actually influence purchase behavior?
faq.a: Yes. Lyrics about self-expression, confidence, and treating yourself cognitively prime customers in a way that supports premium purchasing. The lyrics contribute to the overall atmosphere the same way lighting, displays, and staff tone contribute — they're part of the decision environment.

faq.q: How do you measure whether music is affecting AOV?
faq.a: You need to correlate what played with what customers spent. Entuned logs what played and when, then correlates that data with your floor performance. Over time, you get a clear picture of which sonic parameters move your specific customers toward larger transactions.
